items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Well, when I was playing with him, we had Buddy Petit, and we had all trombone with us. We had Buddy Manatee, we had Zeb Lennaris, and we had Simon the Wild on bass.

ctx.x: Pajot played out there too. Mm-hmm. He had a band out there. But not with Henry Martin, a different time? No, I don't think, I don't think. No. No. Because that was before Pajot's time, you know, see, I imagine. Oh yeah. What about Buddy Petit? Did you remember who played with him much?

Well, when I was playing with him, we had Buddy Petit, and we had all trombone with us. We had Buddy Manatee, we had Zeb Lennaris, and we had Simon the Wild on bass. And he had clarinet, and Zeb Lennaris on clarinet, on trombone. Morris Francis with a René in attire. I can picture the band on the bandstand in the Economy Hall. Hmm. But I can't picture the trombone playing.
And who'd you say was a guitar player, a banjo player? Buddy Manatee. Buddy Manatee and Simon. And Simon. And no piano, of course. No. No violin. No. No.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I know he had Simon Marrera at one time playing with him.

ctx.x: Yeah, the same beat. And they played more than Scott Joplin numbers, you know. See, they played a lot of them. But he wasn't a reading musician, you know. Yeah. Just a routine, as we call it, trumpet player, you know. But he was good, very good. I can't think of who he had in this band. I know he had Simon Marrera at one time playing with him.
He had a lot of different people. He had Zeb and Fred Monroe.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: See, that was his new band, you see. ... Sales, and Simon.

ctx.x: And there's a fine rhythm section. And my buddy had a good rhythm section. Me and Guy A. Butler rap, and a little T-boy, you know, Gilmore, you know, the bass. He had a nice, nice, sometimes Simon, you see. He had a nice rhythm section. Well, the manuals band, you see, I never did hear their band. See, they always played down the Creole, like Ranzami, you know, halls like that.
Perrae, you too? Yeah, yeah, Perrae.
